# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“SO, what is your opinion of them?” Thirza asked.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0000 }

Nell, who was in the gable room, gazed earnestly at three brand-new dresses laid across the bed. The first was made of snuffy colored gingham that Thirza had felt driven to purchase from a peddler during the previous summer owing to its durable appearance; the second was a black-and-white checkered sateen that she had acquired from a bargain counter that winter; and the third was a rigid print featuring an unpleasant tint of blue, bought by her that very week in a Delford store.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0001 }

She was the one who had fashioned them herself, and each of them was constructed in the exact same manner—unadorned skirts gathered densely into unadorned bodices, featuring sleeves that were just as unadorned as the bodices and skirts and as snug as it was possible for sleeves to be.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0002 }

“I will pretend to enjoy them,” Nell stated with gravity.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0003 }

“I am not asking you to picture it,” Thirza stated, her feelings hurt. “Oh, I perceive that you dislike the attire! What is wrong with it? Are the garments not tidy, spotless, and brand-new?”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0004 }

“Yes.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0005 }

“For what reason do you dislike them, then?”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0006 }

“Pretty—they’re—they’re not,” Nell admitted with hesitation.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0007 }

“Pretty!” Thirza expressed with a sniff. “Getting pretty dresses for you was not something I troubled my head about. I do not believe in indulging vanity, Nell, and I will let you know that straight away. Good, sensible, and serviceable are what those dresses are, devoid of any frills or furbelows, and for this summer, they are all that you will receive. School, once you start attending, can be done in the brown gingham and the blue print. For church and Sunday-school, you have the sateen. Keeping them clean, neat, and untorn is what I will expect from you. After the skimpy wincey things that you have been wearing, I should think you would feel grateful to receive almost anything.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0008 }

“Oh, I feel thankful,” Nell declared. “However, my gratitude would be vastly greater had you—had you constructed merely a single one possessing gathered shoulders. Gathered shoulders are the height of style currently. Wearable fabric boasting gathered shoulders would deliver me a supreme rush, Thirza, simply by putting it on.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0009 }

“Well, you must forgo your excitement. I lacked fabric to throw away on puffed sleeves. In any case, I consider them foolish-looking items. My preference is for the simple, practical ones.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0010 }

“Yet I would prefer to seem foolish alongside everyone else instead of simple and practical on my own,” Nell continued in a sorrowful manner.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0011 }

“I know I can rely on you for that! Now, place those dresses neatly on hangers inside your closet, after which you must sit and study the Sunday-school material. A quarterly was obtained from Mr. Bell on your behalf, and your attendance at Sunday-school is expected tomorrow,” declared Thirza, departing for the lower floor in a fit of pique.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0012 }

Nell folded her fingers together and gazed at the garments.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0013 }

“I really hoped for a white dress featuring puffed sleeves,” she murmured gloomily. “I asked God for one, though I didn't actually anticipate it because of that. It didn't seem likely to me that God would take the time to care about the clothing of a small orphan girl. I realized I would simply need to rely on Thirza to get it. Oh well, luckily I have the ability to pretend that a dress among them consists of snow-white muslin adorned with exquisite lace ruffles and triple-puffed sleeves.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0014 }

When the following morning arrived, Thirza was kept from attending Sunday-school alongside Nell because of signs that a sick headache was coming on.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0015 }

“Nell, it will be necessary for you to head downstairs and fetch Mrs. Sowerby,” she stated. “You will be placed in the correct class by her. Now, ensure that you conduct yourself appropriately. Remain behind for the preaching later, and request that Mrs. Sowerby point out our pew to you. This cent is for the collection. Avoid staring at others, and do not squirm. Upon returning home, I expect the text to be recited to me by you.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0016 }

Nell began looking completely respectable, clad in the rigid black-and-white sateen, a garment that was modest concerning its length and surely free from any accusation of being skimpy, yet managed to highlight each corner and angle of her slender frame. Her headwear was a small, flat, shiny, brand-new sailor hat, whose utmost simplicity had similarly greatly let down Nell, who had allowed herself hidden dreams of flowers and ribbon. These blossoms were provided, nonetheless, prior to Nell arriving at the main thoroughfare, because encountering a golden storm of wind-ruffled buttercups and a magnificence of wild roses halfway along the lane, Nell immediately and generously decorated her hat using a dense garland of the flowers. No matter what additional folks may have considered regarding the outcome, it pleased Nell, and she walked briskly down the highway, bearing her red head with its adornment of yellow and pink quite haughtily.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0017 }

Upon arriving at Mrs. Sowerby’s home, she discovered that the lady had already left. Undeterred, Nell continued her journey to the church by herself. Within the porch, she encountered a gathering of small girls, who were all dressed up in varying degrees of bright whites, blues, and pinks, every one of them gazing with inquisitive eyes at this newcomer among them, wearing her bizarre head decoration. The young girls of Brierley were already familiar with strange rumors regarding Nell. Mrs. Sowerby claimed that her temper was terrible; Tobias Buote, the hired farmhand at Grey Shutters, reported that she conversed constantly with herself or addressed the trees and flowers as if she were insane. They observed her and exchanged whispers with one another behind their Sunday school papers. No one offered any welcoming gestures, either at that moment or afterward when the preliminary proceedings concluded and Nell found herself placed in Miss Rogerson’s class.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0018 }

A lady in middle age, Miss Rogerson had spent twenty years teaching a Sunday-school class. The way she taught involved reading the printed questions straight from the quarterly while glaring over its border at whichever little girl she believed should provide the response. Her gaze landed frequently on Nell, who replied without hesitation because Thirza had drilled her so well; nevertheless, it was doubtful whether she truly grasped much regarding the questions or her own replies.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0019 }

She was of the opinion that Miss Rogerson was not to her liking, and her feelings were most unhappy; puffed sleeves were worn by all the other little girls in the class. Life, as Nell perceived it, held no true value if one lacked puffed sleeves.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0020 }

“Well, how did you like Sunday-school?” Thirza inquired upon Nell’s return home. Because her wreath had wilted, Nell had thrown it away in the lane, which temporarily prevented Thirza from discovering it.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0021 }

“I displeased it entirely. It was dreadful.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0022 }

“Nell Harcourt!” Thirza said in a rebuking manner.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0023 }

Releasing a drawn-out sigh, Nell took a seat on the rocking chair, planted a kiss upon a leaf belonging to Bonny, and gave a wave of her hand toward a blooming fuchsia.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0024 }

“It is possible they felt lonely during my absence,” she clarified. “Furthermore, regarding Sunday-school, my conduct was good, exactly as you instructed me. Although Mrs. Sowerby had left, I proceeded on my own. Along with numerous other small girls, I entered the church, and as the preliminary portion took place, my seat was in the pew corner near the window. The prayer delivered by Mr. Bell was exceedingly lengthy. Had I not been positioned beside that window, I would have become terribly fatigued prior to his conclusion. However, because it offered a direct view of the Lake of Glassy Waters, I simply stared at it and envisioned various marvelous scenarios.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0025 }

“You ought not to have done anything like that. You ought to have obeyed Mr. Bell.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0026 }

“However, his words were not directed at me,” Nell objected. “God was the one he addressed, and even then, he appeared to lack much enthusiasm. My impression was that he felt God was located at too great a distance. Suspended above the water was an extensive line of white birches, and the sunlight filtered through their branches, penetrating deeply, deeply into the lake. Oh, Thirza, a gorgeous dream could not have been more lovely! A feeling of excitement went through me, and I simply stated, ‘Thank you for it, God,’ a couple of times.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0027 }

“Only in silence, I trust,” Thirza remarked with concern.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0028 }

“Oh, no, merely under my breath. Well, Mr. Bell finally managed to finish, and I was instructed to enter the classroom alongside Miss Rogerson’s class. Nine other girls were present in it. Puffed sleeves were worn by all of them. I attempted to envision that mine were puffed as well, yet I was unable to do so. Why was I unable to? Envisioning that they were puffed when I was by myself in the east gable was as easy as could be, but doing it there amidst the others who possessed actual, genuine puffs was dreadfully difficult.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0029 }

“Your mind ought not to have dwelt upon your sleeves during Sunday school. Your focus should have been directed toward the lesson instead. I trust you were familiar with it.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0030 }

“Oh, yes; and I responded to a great number of inquiries. Miss Rogerson posed quite a few. It felt unfair to me that she did all the questioning. I desired to ask her numerous things, but I refrained since I felt she was not a kindred spirit. Afterwards, every one of the other little girls recited a paraphrase. She inquired whether I was familiar with any. My reply was that I was not, though I offered to recite, ‘The Dog at His Master’s Grave’ if she wished. It is contained in the Third Royal Reader. Although it is not genuinely religious verse, its sad and melancholy tone makes it practically the same thing. She stated that it was unsuitable and instructed me to memorize the nineteenth paraphrase for the following Sunday. I perused it later while in church, and it is wonderful. Two lines, especially, cause me to feel a real thrill.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0031 }

“‘Fast as the butchered hosts dropped In Midian’s wicked time.’
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0032 }

“I am ignorant of the meaning of ‘squadrons’ and ‘Midian,’ too, but its sound is so tragical. Waiting until next Sunday to recite it is almost impossible for me. During the entire week, I will practice it. Following Sunday-school, I requested Miss Rogerson—since Mrs. Sowerby was located too far off—to point out your pew to me. I remained as motionless as possible, and the text chosen was Revelations, chapter three, verses two and three. That text was exceptionally long. Were I a minister, my choices would be the brief, snappy ones. That sermon went on terribly long, as well. It seems to me the minister was obliged to make it correspond to the text. I failed to find him even slightly interesting. His problem appears to be a lack of sufficient imagination. I gave him very little of my attention. My mind was simply allowed to wander, and I imagined the most astonishing things.”
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0033 }

A sense of powerlessness came over Thirza, knowing a stern reprimand was called for, yet her hands were tied because a portion of Nell’s remarks, particularly those concerning the sermons of the minister and the prayers of Mr. Bell, reflected the very ideas she had harbored in her own innermost soul for a long time without ever voicing them. It appeared to her almost as if those hidden, unspoken, judgmental opinions had abruptly materialized into a tangible and reproachful figure through this candid scrap of forgotten humankind.
{: #nw-v01-c11-p0034 }
